prompt: Some believe that people should not continue to work once they reach the age of retirement. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
There is an ongoing debate about whether people should stop working once they reach the official retirement age. While some argue that retirement should mark the end of an individual’s working life, I disagree with this view because continuing to work can provide both financial and personal benefits.

One compelling reason why people should be allowed to work beyond retirement age is that it can improve their financial security. In many countries, the cost of living has increased considerably, meaning that retirement savings and pensions may not always be sufficient to cover daily expenses. By remaining employed, older people can maintain a stable income and reduce their dependence on family members or government assistance. Furthermore, experienced workers possess valuable knowledge and professional expertise that can benefit younger colleagues. For example, a retired teacher who continues working part-time could mentor new teachers and share decades of practical experience.

Another important advantage is that employment can help older people remain socially active and mentally engaged. Leaving the workplace completely may cause some individuals to feel isolated or lose their sense of purpose. Continuing to participate in professional activities can provide opportunities to communicate with others, learn new skills, and remain productive. However, this does not mean that elderly people should be forced to work. Those who have health problems or simply wish to enjoy their retirement should have the freedom to stop working.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the idea that everyone should stop working when they reach retirement age. Although retirement is an important stage of life, individuals should have the option to continue working if they are physically capable and willing to do so. A flexible retirement system would therefore be more beneficial than imposing a strict age limit.
